name: 13th Floor Coffee
bio:
It’s a family affair! 13th Floor is a speciality coffee stall, brought to you by the End of the Road team. Come say hey and start your day with a silky Flat White, Iced Americano or a tasty treat from a local artisan bakery. We’ll have two stalls again this year – you can find us facing the main campsite and by Joe’s Green.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: 6 O’clock Gin Masterclasses
bio:
Next to Bar Paradiso, Fri-Sun, 12:00 / 14:00 / 16:00

Discover the story behind 6 O’Clock Gin at these free masterclasses led by brand ambassador Tristan Darby. Learn about the Bristol-based distillery, its sustainable approach and its range of gins and liqueurs, with guided tastings, perfect serves and a couple of cocktails along the way.

Spaces are limited, so sign up for a masterclass at the 6 O’Clock Gin stand to reserve your place.

name: AeroPress
bio:
The secret to enjoying delicious coffee anywhere. AeroPress’ 3in1 brewing technology combines immersion, micro-filtration and pressure to deliver a smooth, rich cup, free from bitterness or acidity. Swing by for demos, tasters, or to take advantage of special festival offers. Next to 13th Floor Coffee on the Campsite Run.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Bargello
bio:
Create your own mini stitched masterpiece with bargello embroidery techniques! Learn the basics of bargello and get hooked on this addictive technique. Perfect for new or experienced sewists!

Specifically for adults

name: Barnaby Sykes Pie Maker
bio:
With a love for tradition, history, and the place the pie holds in our nation’s story, Barnaby Sykes provides excellent handmade food that transports people away from the ordinary. Long live the pie!

V, VG, GF

name: Block Printing
bio:
by Om-Baby

Join Studio-om to create beautiful block-printed cotton bunting and pom-poms using fabric remnants from their clothing collection. This fun, family-friendly workshop is suitable for all ages, and your finished bunting can decorate your campsite, buggy or even yourself!

Studio-om works with family-run block-printing workshops in India to produce organic hand-block-printed fabrics, which are transformed into clothing in their London studio. These workshops make creative use of leftover materials, helping ensure every last scrap is put to good use.

Suitable for all ages

name: Born & Raised
bio:
Born & Raised have been serving fresh-to-order sourdough pizzas from the wood-fired oven in their Land Rover Defender since 2012. Their dough is house-made, with ingredients sourced as locally as possible.

V, VG, DF

name: Botanical Print Making with Bristol Print Collective
bio:
Woodland Library area (near the Games Area), Fri – Sun, 11:00 – 14:00.



We are very happy to welcome back Vicky & the Bristol Print Collective to forage in the festival grounds, where they will collect natural forms to create beautiful organic prints! This printmaking process is a wonderful introduction to the spontaneous and playful technique of monoprinting that can be enjoyed by all ages and abilities. Just come along and prepare to get inky!

name: Butterfly Bookmarks
bio:
by Complete Wasters

With a bit of origami folding, create a flapping butterfly or bee. Colour it in with vibrant colours, then pull the tab and watch your creation come to life.

Suitable for all ages

name: Campervan Vintage
bio: Classic vintage with a love for tailored silhouettes and baggy styles alike; think corduroy, dagger collars, double pleats and good quality leather jackets and waistcoats. Sustainability runs through everything Campervan Vintage do, from sourcing (auction houses, church halls and select wholesalers) to selling, restoring and reusing rather than cherry-picking the best pieces.

name: Cantilever
bio: Cantilever, the curated music streaming service, will be at End of the Road for the first time in 2026. Head to their stall, meet the team and try it for yourself. Get a 30 day free trial with code ‘EOTR26’ then £4.99/mo.

name: Ceramic Slug
bio:
The Main Village, Thu, 13:30-18:00 / Fri-Sun, 10:00-18:00

Ceramic Slug is a travelling pottery workshop offering handmade ceramics for sale and the chance to make your own ceramics on-site. Our workshops are run by experienced potters suitable for all levels and ages. Get creative and have your project fired and posted back to you. Come book a spot! www.ceramicslug.co.uk

name: Chick ‘n’ Sours
bio:
London-born, New York and East Asia inspired Chick ’n’ Sours fried chicken is brined, hand-coated in their signature flour blend, twice-fried, then seasoned with their famous Seaweed Crack and served as fully loaded tenders with punchy sauces and toppings.

V, VG, DF

name: Churros Bros
bio:
Churros Bros have been serving up the best churros and chocolate this side of Madrid since 2007. They also use Allpress in Dalston for their fresh roasted coffee. A match made in heaven, or a muddy field.

V, VG, DF

name: Circus Skills
bio:
by Solo Circus & Circus Kaos

The End of the Road Circus Workshop is central to The Wonderlands, where all ages can try their hand at juggling, plate spinning, diabolo, unicycle, hula hoops and more with guidance from our international circus performers.

Suitable for all ages

name: Clay Modelling (Around The Gardens)
bio:
by Far Out Workshops

Drop in over the weekend and help build up our display of clay creations. Animals, monsters, faces, trees – take a few minutes to sit and create with your friends.

name: Collage
bio:
by Indigo Ephemera

Cut, layer and arrange found papers to create your own unique collage. Guided by Indigo Ephemera, this relaxed workshop encourages creative play, unexpected discoveries and conversation as your artwork takes shape.

Suitable for all ages

name: Colourful Centrepiece with Curty Creates
bio:
by Curty Creates

Build a vibrant 3D hanging artwork using cardboard and layers of colourful paper. Experiment with shape, texture and colour to create a striking piece to take home.

Suitable for all audiences

name: Corn Dolly Workshop
bio:
by Vic Jay Art

In these drop-in workshops, you’ll learn to make a small corn dolly – a traditional harvest knot – to take home. Using a simple straw-plaiting technique suitable for most abilities, each 20-minute session also introduces the origins, history and folklore of corn dolly making. Designed to be family-friendly, accessible and inclusive, these relaxed workshops are open to everyone.

Suitable for all ages

name: Crazy Coasters
bio: Make a unique, wacky coaster from a reclaimed tile using decoupage with decorative papers, cut-outs, slogans, comics and more. Seal it to finish, and hey presto – your very own crazy coaster!

name: Crazy Comic Club
bio: A fun comic book and cartooning workshop run by satirical cartoonist James Parsons

name: Croquet
bio:
Near the Healing Gardens, Fri – Sun, 12:00 – 17:00.

Come and enjoy some good old-fashioned ball bashing with Croquet East. Play as a group or make some new friends. We’ll teach you all you need to know about this artful game. Find us hidden between the Garden Stage and the Healing Gardens.

name: Crowns with Curty Creates
bio:
by Curty Creates

Create a fabulously fringed crown using colourful card and a range of accessories to wow your fellow festivalgoers!

name: Doodle With Neil
bio:
by Neil Smith

Join illustrator and graphic designer Neil as he doodles silly cartoons for children of all ages. Grab a pen and some paper, then follow his lead as he shows you how to draw (super furry) animals, monsters, aliens and people using simple, easy-to-follow shapes.

Suitable for all ages

name: Dosa Deli
bio:
Serving homemade, gluten-free, vegetarian South Indian street food, Dosa Deli brings its signature dosa creations to the fields of Dorset. Winners of the Best Vegetarian Dish at the British Street Food Awards and the People’s Choice Award at WOMAD.

V,VG,GF

name: Drama Adventures
bio:
by Acting Out

Acting Out brings high-energy drama adventures to End of the Road, where children invent wild worlds, create unforgettable characters and leap headfirst into stories of their own making. Expect fast-paced games, movement, teamwork, giggles and imaginative fun. Relaxed drop-in sessions welcome children of all confidence levels, whether they love the spotlight or prefer to join in gently. Every session is different. No scripts. No pressure. Just playful storytelling and festival magic.

Aimed at children accompanied by adults

name: Enamelling
bio:
by Medley Arts

Helen is an artist and maker who will help you create amazing jewellery in minutes. Glass enamel powders and beads will be used to apply a fired design to a copper shape. This can then be turned into jewellery of your choice – necklace, badge, earrings or keyring.

Specifically for adults

name: End of The Road Run Club
bio:
Adult Off-Road Run (5K on FRIDAY and 10K on SATURDAY)

5K Run – Meet at Info Point, Fri, 10:00

10K Run – Meet at Info Point, Sat, 10:00

A social off-road trail run out of the festival site, exploring the beautiful and hilly surroundings of Cranborne. This is not a race, but rather a fun run that will allow you to meet like-minded people. Expect around 10/11min mile pace, so do dress appropriately and make sure you’re hydrated as there will be no water points on route. Both runs are limited to 60 runners, and sign-up is required beforehand at the Info Point.

name: Fabazaar
bio: A kaleidoscope of colourful world textiles. Fabazaar’s mix spans block-printed jackets and coats, cotton dresses and shirts, hand-felted children’s gifts, knitted jumpers from Nepal, select pre-loved garments, quilts and homeware.

name: Fable Fox
bio: A Bristol-based clothing and jewellery stall where art meets fashion. Fable Fox’s handmade range spans hand-painted wooden earrings, hand-printed T-shirts, embroidered pendants and crochet garments, plus trousers and shorts made in-house.

name: General Painting
bio:
Grab a paintbrush and let your imagination take over. Whether you’re creating a masterpiece or simply enjoying the process, this is a relaxed space to experiment with colour, make a little mess and add your artwork to the growing gallery.

Suitable for all audiences

name: Giant Mural
bio:
by Spare Room Arts

Use colour, shapes, paint and your imagination to create a shared mural. Paint whatever you like, or follow the existing lines and add your own ideas. There are no rules and no right or wrong way—just creativity. Every colour, mark and shape becomes part of the growing artwork.

Suitable for all ages

name: Goodness Gracious
bio:
Veggie and vegan dishes served from a beautiful Saddlespan marquee and cooked by a Lebanese chef from the northern city of Akkar. Try the fatayer (hand-made filo parcels filled with fresh spinach and feta) and batata hara (spicy potatoes).

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Guasa Arepas
bio:
Pioneers of Venezuelan street food, Guasa return to End of the Road with gluten-free arepas – toasted buns packed with slow-cooked meats, slaws and delicious homemade sauces.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Hakkō House
bio:
Hakkō House serve umami-rich dishes inspired by fermentation and old family recipes. Their unique menu – featuring Ōkī Makī rolls (burrito-maki fusion), Kara-age Chicken, and plant-based Miso Soup – offers a flavourful, health-conscious twist on Japanese cuisine.

V,VG,GF

name: Hanoi Kitchen
bio:
Having scoured Hanoi’s streets and tasted every dish along the way, Hanoi Kitchen persuaded their favourites to share trade secrets, bringing the very best Vietnamese street food to you. They stay true to the flavours of Hanoi, with the occasional signature twist. Dishes strike the perfect balance of hot, spicy, fresh and fragrant, ensuring there is something for everyone, including Bún Pots and Banh-Mi.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Headlock Vintage Clothing
bio: Vintage clothing for every layer. Headlock’s rails are packed with cable knit jumpers, check shirts, Chore jackets and workwear, plus rain-ready Berghaus and North Face jackets, and plenty more to dig through.

name: How Does It Feel To Be Loved? (Children’s Disco)
bio:
The Boat, Sun, 09:30-11:00

How Does It Feel To Be Loved? is an indie pop and soul club which has been running in London since 2002. We first held our children’s version of HDIF at End of the Road in 2011, which led to the HDIF Family Disco starting in London in 2018. If you fancy dancing to Belle & Sebastian, Ramones, Pixies, David Bowie, Camera Obscura, Allo Darlin’ and a ton of soul and ‘60s smashes with your family, then join us at The Boat on Sunday morning.

name: Hughes Fresh Fruit
bio:
A family-run business established in 1983, Hughes Fresh Fruit serves fresh fruit, fruit salads and ice-cold whole-fruit smoothies at festivals and events across the UK. Fruit is sourced as locally as possible, with organic and Fairtrade produce used wherever available.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Hula Hoop
bio:
by Jasmin Circus

Get into a spin with Jasmin, a circus artist specialising in multi-hoop. Bringing the magic of hoops to End of the Road, Jasmin invites participants of all levels to discover the joy of movement, coordination and play. Whether you’re a complete beginner or a budding pro, come along to find your flow and learn some new tricks!

Suitable for all ages

name: HungaMunga’s Modern Art Menagerie
bio:
by Hunga Munga

HungaMunga, the London-based group of artists, musicians and performers, is celebrating 20 years of arty fun – just like End of the Road. Let’s all meet up in the year 2026… to paint, make and create artwork inspired by the music and visuals of Pulp, in celebration of Jarvis and co. Think retro disco and party décor, Pop Art, pin-ups, collage and iconic album covers – or simply express yourself!

Suitable for all ages

name: Ice Green
bio:
A vintage caravan serving handmade vegan gelato, from classics to the unexpected. Made using ethically sourced, foraged oat, coconut, almond, peanut and hazelnut milks, around 80% is gluten-free, with gluten-free cones available. It’s solar-powered on-site – the sun keeps the scoops chilled!

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Instant Songs of Kindness
bio:
by Natural Causes

Come and create brand new songs together, with every idea coming from you. Choose a title, pick a letter to set the key, craft the lyrics, dance the tempo and holler the tune. Form a band where every idea is welcomed, and watch joy and music come to life in an instant.

Suitable for all ages

name: Iron Born Barbershop
bio: Iron Born Barbershop is on hand for a proper tidy-up, whatever state your hair’s in after a few days under canvas.

name: Kids Movement Club
bio:
by Hayley Yoga

One hour of physical, kid-led, imaginative, creative play for children and their grown-ups with youth leader and yoga teacher, Hayley Yoga. A creative space outside of demands where we’ll be creating environments through props, sound, fabric, narrative and movement – encouraging connections to our bodies, imaginations and each other!

C: Aimed at children accompanied by adults

name: Kinky Melon’s Retro Boutique
bio: Owned by Jon & Vix, a couple with a life-long passion for vintage clothing. Their stock is lovingly hand-picked, freshly laundered and fairly priced – mostly sourced within a 20 mile radius of home, with sustainability at heart. Friendly, well turned-out and set in a 1970s boutique-themed pitch, a visit here is often called a memorable part of the festival experience.

name: Kubb
bio:
Folly Games Area, Fri – Sun, 14:00 – 18:00.

Pit yourself against friends or strangers and give your throwing arm a good workout with a spot of Viking Kubb. Played for over 1000 years on the Baltic island of Gotland (and for 20 years at End of the Road), Swedish Kubb (or Viking Chess) is a game that finds itself somewhere between horseshoes and bowling.

name: La Crêperie
bio:
Sweet and savoury French crêpes, gluten-free buckwheat galettes and Fairtrade organic coffee. La Crêperie has been a UK festival stalwart since 1989, priding themselves on using high-quality produce and homemade batters.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Lalita’s
bio:
Lalita’s bring authentic South Indian street food that’s 100% vegan, gluten-free and ethically produced. Expect vibrant dishes, including paratha masala, masala vada, idli sambar, aloo bonda and thalis, to satisfy your curry cravings in the absence of The Curry Shed, who we bid a fond farewell and happy retirement.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Little Wildlings
Loki Poké
bio:
Award-winning poké bowls piled with veg, fresh proteins, pickles, sauce and crunchy toppings, all served on seasoned sushi rice. Gluten-free, with sustainably sourced fish, organic chicken.

VG, GF, DF

name: Lola’s Fish and Chips
bio: Born from a humble fish shack in South East London, Lola’s is all about good, ethically sourced ingredients, simply prepared fish and cooking to perfection. Their vans – with a beach hut-inspired aesthetic – are a slice of English seaside.

name: Lucy & Yak
bio: Lucy & Yak are back, bringing their famous pink pop-up bus loaded with colourful dungarees, “Imperfect Yaks,” and summer essentials.

name: Made of Dough
bio:
Made of Dough is a street food outfit passionate about music, festivals and great pizza. Hand-stretched, slow-proofed, 48-hour-fermented dough gives their pizzas a light, airy crust. Cooked fresh to order, their pizzas were named Top London Pizzeria 2026 by BBC Food.

V, DF

name: Magic and Games
bio:
by Come To My Party

Kerry from Come To My Party offers a family-friendly performance blending singing, magic, and games. The show invites children and their grown-ups to gather, join in, and share a little wonder together.

Aimed at children accompanied by adults

name: Makatcha
bio:
Makatcha is a family-run Indonesian curry stall serving up moreish Rendang and their famous coconut chicken. All dishes are cooked from scratch using the best ingredients (no preservatives of any kind).

VG, GF, DF

name: Mamacha Alpaca Knitwear
bio: Alpaca knitwear designed by Mamacha and made in a women’s cooperative in Lima, Peru. As a not-for-profit, they provide reliable income for women in impoverished areas of northern Lima, using only 100% alpaca yarn. Hats, gloves, scarves and socks are hand-knitted and signed by the knitter, while two basic knitting machines turn out their popular jumpers, ponchos, legwarmers and throws.

name: Million Headed Monster
bio: A British heritage headwear brand specialising in flat caps and hats made from traditional tweeds and natural fabrics. Gamble & Gunn work closely with historic mills and small fabric producers to craft classic flat caps, baker boys, fedoras and seasonal styles in premium wool tweeds, linens and cottons that are built for comfort and longevity. They also stock sunglasses, waterproofs, vintage blankets and some clothing for festival goers.

name: Mindful Botanical Sketching
bio:
by Gemma Hastilow

Slow down and discover the intricate beauty of late-summer native plants. Using a mix of locally foraged specimens and detailed photography to help protect rare species, you’ll create a beautiful page of illustrated nature notes. We’ll focus on seasonal treasures including knapweed, wild marjoram, scabious and yarrow. Beginners and all ages are welcome.

Specifically for adults

name: Mixed Up Dolly
bio: Unique, handcrafted clay and resin jewellery and accessories, all made by hand in Wells, Somerset. Expect whimsical, fun pieces – many inspired by food and drink, with miniature versions of everyday items designed to appeal to all ages and genders.

name: MorMor
bio:
MorMor is an award-winning, critically acclaimed Middle Eastern street food, mezze and small plates kitchen that brings you health-conscious, flavour-bursting dishes inspired by the cuisines and cultures of the Levant.

V, VG, GF

name: Morning Glory
bio:
OBSESSED with breakfast!? Think huge Breakfast Burritos, Loaded Hash Browns, Ultimate Brekkie Sarnies, OJ and damn fine coffee. Vegan/gluten-free? They’ve got your back with alternatives for most of their menu. Look for the neon “bacon” sign in the campsite!

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Neem
bio: Joining us for the very first time this year, Neem is here to elevate your festival wardrobe with modern, carbon-neutral menswear crafted from recycled materials. Perfect for the 6 Music Dad looking to swap basics and band T-shirts for effortless, casual elegance, their pieces prove fatherhood and great taste belong together.

name: Open Sesame
bio:
Persian-inspired street food cooked with care. Open Sesame invent new dishes all the time – rooted in the bold spices, freshness and generosity of Middle Eastern cuisine, often slow-cooked, grilled or smoked to perfection. They use specialist, authentic ingredients alongside locally sourced produce from Devon wherever possible.

V, GF, DF

name: Oxfords Bakery Ltd
bio:
Artisan Bakery stand, selling freshly baked morning goods, croissants, savouries, including vegan sausage rolls and sourdough, with wheat grown in Tarrant Launceston, across the field from the festival! Morning coffee and a croissant, anyone?!

V, VG

name: Paellaria
bio:
Paelleria’s kick-ass, award-winning paella is made entirely on-site using only the finest Spanish ingredients, sourced and imported from Valencia, Spain.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Paletas
bio:
Paletas offer handmade, natural Mexican-style ice lollies made with whole fruit, creating a variety of delicious traditional and non-traditional flavours.

V, VG, GF

name: Parachute Games
bio:
by Danny Annaly

Come and join Danny the Parachute for fun and games beneath the parachute! We’ll play all the classics – Cat and Mouse, Sharks, Rollercoaster, Mushroom Mountain, Washing Machine and Danny’s favourite, Popcorn. Ever made popcorn on a giant parachute with thirty people? Come along, make new friends and join the fun!

Aimed at children accompanied by adults

name: Pieminister
bio:
Award-winning pies, made using responsibly sourced ingredients – including free-range British meat and innovative plant-based alternatives – lovingly made since 2003 by the recently B Corp certified Bristol stalwarts Pieminister.

V, VG, DF

name: Piggie Smalls
bio:
Crispy duck, various ways, freshly cooked in their beautiful gold airstream.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Play/Forest School
bio:
by Flowt

Inspired by the elements – Earth, Water, Wind and Fire – these sessions begin with eco-conscious storytelling expressed through guided movement and dance, before creating large collaborative artworks using natural materials.

Play/Forest School – Earth (C)

Craft your own paintbrushes and explore mark-making using earth as paint, with expansive gestures and full-body expression.

Play/Forest School – Water (C)

Explore balance, fluid movement and gravity before translating these ideas into collaborative artwork.

Play/Forest School – Wind & Fire (C)

Work with breath, rhythm and movement through sun salutations, then create artwork inspired by breath and earth pigments.

Aimed at children accompanied by adults

name: Poster Stall
bio:
Joe’s Green

The UK Poster Association (UKPA) is a collective of independent artists and screen printers, founded to champion the vibrant world of screen-printed gig poster art. A global phenomenon, these hand-crafted posters occupy a unique space between advertisement and artefact – lovingly made documents that celebrate the events, bands and music they commemorate.

The UKPA returns to this year’s End of the Road Festival, presenting a curated selection of limited-edition prints created exclusively for the event, alongside existing work by UKPA artists Graham Pilling, Luke Drozd, Paul Kelly, and Tommy Davidson-Hawley. Here you will find this year’s lineup poster, along with a limited edition poster celebrating 20 years of End of the Road!

name: Poster Stall
bio:
Joe’s Green

The UK Poster Association (UKPA) is a collective of independent artists and screen printers, founded to champion the vibrant world of screen-printed gig poster art. A global phenomenon, these hand-crafted posters occupy a unique space between advertisement and artefact – lovingly made documents that celebrate the events, bands and music they commemorate.

The UKPA returns to this year’s End of the Road Festival, presenting a curated selection of limited-edition prints created exclusively for the event, alongside existing work by UKPA artists.

name: Punch Needle
bio:
by Darn It Workshops

The most wholesome fun you can have punching something! This craft combines rug-making and embroidery to create something squishy and tactile.

Specifically for adults

name: Pura Vida
bio:
Pura Vida is back with a fresh new look, selling vegan and vegetarian Mexican street food made on-site with fresh whole foods. From breakfast Burritos to irresistible Nachos. Everything can be made gluten-free and vegan – just pop by and ask!

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Qigong
bio:
by Magpie Qi Gong

Qigong, meaning “energy cultivation”, is the ancient practice that gave rise to Tai Chi. Combining mindful movement, breathing, stretching, posture and meditation, it offers a gentle way to energise body and mind.

A festival favourite since 2006, Shiatsu practitioner and Qigong instructor Mark will lead relaxed, Taoist-inspired morning sessions rooted in Chinese medicine.

Suitable for all ages

name: Recycled Fabric Headdresses
bio:
by Spare Room Arts

Design and create your own unique festival headdress using recycled satins and pre-loved fabrics. This much-loved End of the Road activity invites you to play with colour, texture and creativity while giving beautiful materials a new life.

Suitable for all ages

name: Redleb Jewellery
bio: Handmade contemporary silver and gold jewellery, crafted from Eco silver and gold with ethically sourced semi-precious gemstones. Redleb also work industrial waste into their pieces; think surfite, sea glass, graffitite, recycled copper, acrylic and brass.

name: Roaming Rotisserie
bio:
The most succulent chicken, cooked on a rotisserie above a tray of crispy roasted potatoes, slowly infused by the juices. A French market (and End of the Road) favourite.

DF

name: Rough Trade
bio: An iconic cornerstone of independent music culture since 1976, Rough Trade brings its curated selection of vinyl, CDs, and exclusive merch to End of the Road. Drop by the pop-up shop throughout the weekend to browse the finest new releases, festival gems, and catch exclusive artist signing sessions.

name: Rounders
bio:
Folly Games Area, Fri-Sun, 11:00-14:00

​​Looking for an exciting and active way to get into the swing of things at End of the Road? Then come and step up to the plate for a thrilling game of rounders! Whether you’re a young player looking to show off your skills or looking for a fun way to shake off last night’s antics, we’ve got all bases covered. We promise to give you a pitch-perfect morning before the music begins, with prizes to be won and a friendly atmosphere guaranteed to catch your attention.

name: Routes Coffee
bio:
Routes Coffee began when two best friends travelled back to the UK from Australia with a newfound love for good coffee. On their journey home, they stopped in over 30 countries, learning from farmers, distributors, roasters and baristas.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Saint Valentines Liquorice Company
bio: The best quality liquorice you can find, served with love from their 4.5m stall – a little taste of devotion for liquorice lovers.

name: Sam’s Real Fudge
bio:
Hand-made and proper crumbly, Sam’s Real Fudge comes in 15+ flavours, with a range of vegan options too.

(V, VG)

name: Sara Withers & Xuella Arnold
bio: Jewellery designed and made by Sara Withers and Xuella Arnold – same little marquee as always.

name: Screen Printing
bio:
by Jon Mackay

Jon Mackay designs and hand prints posters for bands, venues and events. Commissions have included The Lumineers, Johnny Flynn, Bastille, Band Of Horses, Bear’s Den and many more. He will guide you in creating a stencil and then printing it onto paper or a bag.

Suitable for all ages

name: Secret Post Office
bio:
The Main Village



Whether you’re decorating postcards, taking your photo or writing love letters, the Secret Post Office will help you get the message out. Mark your post with a delivery time, an address (campsite/tent colour), a description of the recipient and their general whereabouts, and our hardworking posties will deliver. They are constantly out on rounds, delivering the mail with the help of their bicycles, post trolleys, and megaphones. Please note, there will also be a post box in or next to the EOTR Merch Shop that is for outgoing mail- please do not post your Secret mail in here.

name: Shaboutique
bio: Upcycled clothing and accessories made in Brighton, alongside bags crafted from ring-pulls in support of Filipino charity PCF, and Fairtrade crochet earrings from a female collective in Turkey.

name: Shadow Arts with Curty Creates
bio:
by Curty Creates

Experiment with colour, paint and card to create bold symmetrical designs and playful shadow effects. A hands-on workshop that encourages creativity, curiosity and plenty of colourful experimentation.

Suitable for all ages

name: Shepherds Ice Cream Parlour
bio:
Serving up smooth, creamy sheep’s milk gelato, delicious dairy-free ice creams, and real fruit sorbets made with spring water, Shepherds is a real festival favourite for kids and adults alike.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Shilpa Silver
bio: A family-run stall with real character and a vibrant presence. Shilpa Silver brings together an eclectic collection from Central America – unusual silver and copper jewellery, Mexican folk art and Guatemalan textiles. Their contemporary Mexican silver, bronze and copper pieces are personally chosen from small family businesses and independent designers.

name: Smoking Buns
bio:
Delicious UK-reared dry-aged chuck steak patties, smoky pulled pork-filled brioche buns, fresh bread by Hobbs House Bakery (gluten-free available), plus options for vegans and veggies too – like their new caramelised mushroom and garlic burger. They’re open for breakfast until the small hours, so you can always get your fix!

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Spoon Carving
bio:
The Main Village, Fri – Sun, 10:00 – 17:00.

During this informative and fun two-hour workshop, you will carve yourself your very own wooden spoon. You’ll also learn the skills and techniques to make more in the future. All materials and tools provided. Advanced booking at the stall once you are on-site is recommended due to limited spaces.

name: Story Bicycle
bio:
by Isabella Necessity

Isabella Necessity loves to share tales from her incredible bicycling adventures through the wilds of the world. When the doors of her story box swing open, she’ll whisk you away on magical adventures filled with bravery, wonder and delight.

From the oak woods of the West Country to the rainforests of Brazil, Isabella’s earthy charm will put a skip in your step and hope in your heart. With engaging storytelling, quirky puppets and beautifully hand-drawn illustrations, expect moments of magic, plenty of fun and a wonderful tale well told.

Inspired by the Japanese art of kamishibai, meaning “paper theatre”, Isabella Necessity is the alter ego of Sara Hurley, one of the UK’s leading kamishibai performers.

Aimed at children accompanied by adults

name: Storysmith Bookshop
bio:
The Main Village (opposite the Big Top)

Joining us again this year is award-winning Bristol book shop Storysmith, bringing their unique offering to End of the Road. Experts at finding the most beautiful, unusual and irresistible books, all perfectly presented by their knowledgeable young booksellers. It’s the perfect spot to browse hundreds of titles and catch author signings from our Literature lineup. www.storysmithbooks.com

name: String Art Cards
bio:
by Darn It Workshops

Using geometric templates, we’ll create hand-stitched string art cards that are striking and easy to keep going with. This technique takes inspiration from 70s string art using nails on wood, adapted to card making.

Specifically for adults

name: The Bhaji Shack
bio:
Lightly spiced bhajis deep-fried to crispy perfection. Plus paneer and fresh salads, all served in flatbreads or bowls and accompanied with their signature toppings: mint raita, curry mayo, pickled onions, mango chutney and fresh herbs.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: The Fields
bio: Vintage made modern. The Fields hand-dye pure wool blankets and cushions in indigo patterns and bright colours, alongside decorations, bunting, broaches and crowns felted from scraps and fleece from their own tiny flock of rare breed sheep. Look out for indigo-dyed Aran jumpers, fully restored vintage armchairs, and true 60s/70s deckchairs reupholstered in original florals and stripes.

name: The Helter Skelter
bio:
Folly Games Area. Thurs, 13:30 – 21:00. Fri – Sun, 10:00 – 21:00. £4 a slide.

Adults can accompany children under 1.1M tall for free if going down the slide together.

name: The Hippy Chippy
bio:
Over 20 years of festival catering have gone into making some of the best chips you’ll ever try. Triple-cooked to perfection and still the only UK festival chip seller making chips from potatoes on site.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: The Line Of Best Fit Pop-Up Performances
bio: If you time things right, a wander into the woods could mean catching a secret, intimate performance from one of your favourite bands. A drop-in at the Piano Stage could mean witnessing a rare one-off collaboration or a rare Q&A. Any of these things could mean you’ve stumbled across one of the surprise shows curated by award-winning music website The Line Of Best Fit.

name: The Ninth Wave Clothing Company
bio: An own-brand clothing company based in Wales. The Ninth Wave make fleeces, dresses, trousers, shirts, sweatshirts, bags and shorts, all crafted from recycled, deadstock and sustainably sourced fabrics.

name: The Pit Shop
bio: Convenience goods and camping equipment store

name: The Plant Cafe
bio:
The Plant Cafe (in the Healing Gardens) serves fresh food celebrating seasonal, nourishing ingredients. Each day presents freshly made salads, alongside homemade cakes and barista coffee.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: The Silent Disco
bio:
The Folly Stage, Thurs, 23:30 – 03:00. The Singing Theatre, Fri & Sat, 23:30 – LATE



Two DJs battle for your attention through wireless headphones late into the night. From old-school soul to ‘80s classics and modern pop – The Headphone Disco decks will be spinning beneath the stars once again at The Singing Theatre. Wandering into the woods with tunes in your ears is going to be mighty tempting, so there will be a £10 returnable deposit required upfront and signage to keep you in rangelease note: no change can be given). If you forget to return your Silent Disco headphones on the night, you will be responsible for returning the headphones by post to claim a refund. You should contact info@endoftheroadfestival.com after the festival with your query.

name: The Tea Stop
bio:
The Tea Stop is a lovingly converted vintage bus serving comfort, nostalgia and a proper good brew. Start your morning with what many call the best triple-rasher sandwich on site, drop by for afternoon tea and cake, or a warming midnight hot chocolate.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: The Toastie Temple
bio:
The Toastie Temple serves freshly roasted, Fairtrade, organic, Rainforest Alliance coffee, loose-leaf teas and vegan Fairtrade hot chocolate. Their organic, gluten-free oat milk suits dietary needs without compromising flavour. They also offer sourdough toasties, cakes, sugar-free soft drinks, and kombucha.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: The Vintage Co-op
bio: A merry band of vintage traders from all over the UK, coming together each summer to offer a magical medley of vintage treasures and handcrafted creations.

name: The Whole Cheese
bio:
Founded in 2012 and on a mission to spread the good word of cheese, The Wholecheese grills melty classics from small West Country producers, alongside Little Jack’s award-winning sausage rolls and Bristol Twenty coffee. Try the Bath blue and chutney.

V, VE

name: Third Man Records
bio: The Third Man Records Stall serves as an immersive physical haven for vinyl junkies and casual listeners alike. Curated with the tactile obsessiveness that defines the brand, the pop-up offers an exclusive range of rare physical releases, direct-to-acetate pressings, limited-edition festival merchandise, and Third Man Books titles.

name: Thyme & Tide
bio:
Thyme & Tide showcases Chef Lee Lake’s travel-inspired, vibrant and healthy seafood. Sustainably and locally sourced Cornish fish fill delicious Cajun Fish Burgers, Whitebait and their highly sought-after Scallop and Bacon breakfast roll.

V, GF, DF

name: Tibetan Kitchen
bio:
Authentic Himalayan food, cooked on-site with high-quality ingredients. This wonderful menu includes handcrafted ‘momo’ steamed dumplings stuffed with British beef or mixed vegetables, hearty curries and sizzling stir-fries.

V, VG, GF

name: Tongue ‘N Cheek
bio:
An incredible range of sandwiches from burgers to steak and fries to Japanese fried chicken, plus rosemary and truffle & parmesan fries. Vegetarian options are available.

VG, GF, DF

name: Upcycled Fabric Patches
bio:
by Weaving Change

Join us in making an End of the Road upcycled fabric patch using lino printing, embroidery and beading techniques. Run by Weaving Change, a Bristol-based organisation on a mission to slow down fast fashion, this welcoming workshop celebrates simple skills, reuse and creative self-expression. No experience is needed, and all materials are provided.

Specifically for adults

name: Velo Domestique
bio:
Calling all cyclists! Say hi to Velo Domestique, an independent cycle café from Dorset, serving high-quality coffee, cakes, breakfast tacos, and other hot drinks.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Videopia
bio:
The Main Village

Ever wanted to be in the movies? Well, here’s your chance! Videopia is an interactive movie-making activity that casts, shoots and screens tributes to Hollywood classics with you in the starring role. Videopia will be roaming the grounds of Larmer Tree Gardens recruiting festival-goers to star in a very silly version of the cult classic – Ghostbusters! The footage will be screened in the Videopia tent at the end of each day, before being uploaded to their YouTube channel, so you can relive your on-screen glory once you get home.

name: Vintage Relics Vinyl Records
bio: Seconds hand vinyl records.

name: Wake Up Singing
bio:
by Wake Up Singing

Songs of all shapes and sizes, warming up, breathing together, humming, shaking and laughing. Songs from all over the place, rounds and chants, songs to make you laugh, wake up and relax.

Specifically for adults

name: Where Is My Mind? Quiz
bio:
Cider Bus Tent, Sun, 13:00 – 14:30ish

Just as you’ve come to expect, it’s the usual music and pop-culture quiz – but with the festival celebrating its 20th edition this year, expect a few questions delving into End of the Road’s history too! Teams of up to eight are welcome, and everyone (except previous winners – fair’s fair!) is in the running for the grand prize: a pair of End of the Road 2027 passes.

name: Whole Food Heaven Buddha Bowls
bio:
Serving their legendary Buddha Bowls since 2010, Whole Food Heaven offers delicious vegetarian, vegan, dairy-free, wheat and gluten-free dishes made with high-quality, unrefined ingredients and organic produce wherever possible.

V, VG, GF, DF

name: Wholesome Junkies
bio: Wholesome Junkies is an award-winning, Manchester-based plant-based street food kitchen serving bold, indulgent burgers and sides that are big on flavour.

name: Wild Lino Printing
bio:
by Gemma Hastilow

Discover the rhythmic, relaxing art of printmaking. Gemma will guide you through designing, carving and hand-printing your own lino block. No drawing skills? No problem. You’ll leave with a finished print and the skills to keep carving at home. Please note there is a materials charge for this session.

name: Wiltshire Hurdles
bio:
The Main Village, Fri-Sun, 10:00-17:00



Watch hurdle-making demonstrations or have a go yourself. Make a walking stick using the shave horse and drawknife. Take a look at our information boards and have a chat about conservation and woodland management.

name: Woodland Workshops by The Larmer Tree Project
bio:
Join us for three days of creativity inspired by the fairy tale magic of the Larmer Tree Gardens. Through art, poetry, and stitching, we will create stories, costumes, textiles, and poems using reclaimed, gathered, and foraged materials. All ages welcome. No experience necessary.

Family Art Workshop: Fairies, Djinns and Dragons

Friday, Saturday & Sunday: 10:00 – 12:00

Drop-in workshop creating headdresses and puppets celebrating the fairy tales from the gardens

Poetry from the Garden: Poetry Workshop

Friday, Saturday & Sunday: 13:00 – 15:00

Stitching the Peackock’s Tale: Collaborative Textile Artwork

Friday, Saturday & Sunday: 15:00 – 17:00

Creation of the Larmer Poetry Tree & Collaborative Textile Artwork –

The Peacock’s Tale

Ongoing throughout the festival

name: Yoga for Adults
bio:
by Hayley Yoga

Ease into the day with a gentle morning flow. Expect a caring, welcoming session with wake-up and shake-up moments, humour and gentle discovery. Yoga asana, breathwork and self-massage come as standard, all in an invitational, consent-led space, set to the soundtrack of nature (and perhaps an early Garden Stage soundcheck!).
